pieces.title: The 180-degree rule and the 360-degree room
pieces.caption: Two people at a low table, seen from above. Hollywood keeps every camera on one side of the line between them. Ozu sets the camera anywhere in the room. *What is real and what is a choice:* The eight positions are a drawing choice; the page claims only that he crosses the axis routinely.

challenge.by: challenger · light round, batch D (drawn diagrams) · read-only dispatch

verdicts.file: Yasujirō Ozu — rich — the 180-degree rule and the 360-degree room.svg
verdicts.why: The 180-degree rule is drawn correctly: the axis runs through the two sitters, all three Hollywood cameras sit on one side, the other half is hatched "the camera never comes here", and "left stays left" follows. The Ozu half says what the sentence says (crosses the axis; shape to shape, not eye to eye). Note: the caption's "sets the camera anywhere in the room" is more than the page's "crosses ... routinely"; the honest line admits it, so change the word to "on either side of the line".
